data.gender_notes: Vitalina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'vitalis', meaning 'living' or 'full of life'. In Christian tradition, Vitalina can also refer to the name of a saint. The name Vitalina carries the meaning “Life” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Vitalina usually hope their child will grow to embody life and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the gift of life and the importance of living each day to the fullest.
data.etymology: Vitalina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Life.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vitalina total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: ויטלינה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם ויטלינה נגזר מלטינית ומשמעותו חיים או קשור לחיים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ויטלינה הוא נגזר מהמילה הלטינית 'ויטאליס' (Vitalis), שפירושה 'של חיים' או 'קשור לחיים'. השם קשור למושג החיים הנצחיים והוא משמש לעתים קרובות בקשר לנצרות, שכן הוא מבטא את הרעיון של חיים רוחניים ויחסים עם אלוהים. השימוש בשם זה במסגרת הנצרות הוא בעיקר בקרב קהילות שמדברות שפות רומאניות ומשפחות נוצריות אירופיות.

in_greek.name: Βιταλίνα
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Βιταλίνα σημαίνει ζωή ή που σχετίζεται με τη ζωή
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Βιταλίνα προέρχεται από τη λατινική λέξη 'Vitalis', που σημαίνει 'της ζωής' ή 'που σχετίζεται με τη ζωή'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόλο που δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά, ο όρος ζωής έχει πνευματική σημασία, αναφερόμενος στη ζωή μετά θάνατον και την πνευματική αναγέννηση. Ο όρος χρησιμοποιείται συχνά στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία για να εκφράσει την αιώνια ζωή και τη σχέση με τον Θεό. Στον ελληνικό πολιτισμό, το όνομα Βιταλίνα συνδέεται με την έννοια της ζωής και της πνευματικής αναζήτησης.

in_latin.name: Vitalina
in_latin.meaning: The name Vitalina means of life or related to life
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Vitalina derives from the Latin word 'Vitalis', meaning 'of life' or 'related to life'. In the context of early Christianity, the concept of life was closely tied to eternal life and spiritual rebirth. The name Vitalina reflects the importance of spiritual life and the pursuit of a relationship with God. Historically, the name has been used in Christian communities to signify a connection to the divine and the eternal nature of the soul.

in_english.name: Vitalina

in_english.long_meaning: The name Vitalina originates from the Latin 'Vitalis', meaning 'of life' or 'related to life'. Vitalina symbolizes spiritual vitality, renewal, and a deep connection to one's faith. In modern usage, Vitalina remains a meaningful choice for Christian families seeking a name that embodies their spiritual values.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vitalina holds an enduring allure and charm due to its Latin roots, which evoke a sense of energy, vitality, and liveliness. Its associations with the vibrant culture of the Roman Empire can lend an owner of the name a rich historical and artistic background.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name Vitalina acknowledges the divine gift of life and vitality given to us by God. By bearing this name, one may be reminded to cherish each moment and live a life full of purpose, love, and faith. The name also pays homage to St. Vitalis, a martyr known for his faith and strength, reminding its bearer to embody these virtues in their own lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vitalina: Life-giving, bearing and nurturing the essence of life. A beacon of hope and strength, reminding us of the vitality and resilience of the human spirit.

historical_references.reference: Vitalis was a third-century martyr venerated in the Roman Catholic Church. He was a soldier who was beheaded during the persecution of Maximian Hercules in 304 AD for refusing to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods.
historical_references.context: Roman Catholic Church, Maximian Hercules persecution

historical_references.reference: Vitalis and Hippolyta were two young Christians who were martyred in Africa during the persecution of Diocletian in 304 AD. They were betrothed to each other and were put to death together when they refused to renounce their faith.

modern_usage.modern_context: Vitalina is a Lithuanian-born, Ukrainian actress who gained international recognition for her role in the 2019 Ukrainian film 'Dykana' (The Wound). She has been praised for her powerful performances in Ukrainian cinema, particularly in the New Wave Cinema movement and Eastern European art house films. Vitalina's work has been showcased on popular streaming platforms like Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Mubi, making her accessible to a wider audience and contributing to the growing trend of independent films from Eastern Europe gaining mainstream recognition.
